papers.title: scYeast: a biological-knowledge-guided foundation model on yeast single-cell transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Though large-scale pre-trained models are vital for foundational cell modeling, most of them focus on human or mouse systems, with less emphasis on model organisms like yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae), and fail to use existing biological prior knowledge effectively. Here, we present scYeast, the first foundational cell model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics that effectively embeds biological priors. scYeast employs a novel asymmetric parallel architecture to infuse transcriptional regulatory information into the Transformer's attention mechanism, leveraging biological knowledge during tr
papers.summary: The authors present scYeast, the first foundation model for yeast single-cell transcriptomics, which integrates biological prior knowledge (transcriptional regulatory information) into a Transformer architecture via an asymmetric parallel design. This approach improves cell modeling by leveraging known biology, addressing a gap in models focused mainly on human or mouse systems.

papers.title: Characterizing highly conserved fragments in 3'UTRs via statistical and transfer learning approaches.
papers.abstract: 3' Untranslated regions (3'UTRs) serve as regulatory platforms that modulate steps in the central dogma through the binding of RNA-binding proteins and miRNAs. Their binding sites are often identified through orthologous regions among species. A separate but related discovery was the ultraconserved elements (UCEs) detected in human, rat, and mouse genomes two decades ago. However, knowledge about their functions is limited. Perplexingly, mutagenesis of UCEs produced no observable phenotypic differences. The majority of UCEs are non-coding, though ∼8% are located in the 3'UTRs. Given the import
papers.summary: This study characterizes highly conserved fragments within 3' untranslated regions (3'UTRs) using statistical and transfer learning approaches, linking them to ultraconserved elements (UCEs) and potential regulatory functions. The findings provide new insights into the functional significance of conserved non-coding elements, which have previously shown no observable phenotypic effects upon mutagenesis.

papers.title: Machine learning-based molecular detection using dark-field observation of two different nanoparticles.
papers.abstract: Metal nanoparticles, such as gold nanoparticles (AuNPs), are widely used as biosensing materials. In previous studies, dark-field microscopy (DFM) has been utilised to examine target-induced AuNP aggregation for molecular sensing. The intensity of scattering light of each spot observed by DFM was analysed at the single-cluster level for sensitive molecular detection. However, changes in the intensity and colour of AuNP aggregates were not significant when the inter-particle distance was large because of the insufficient effect of the surface plasmon resonance, suggesting difficulty in the sens
papers.summary: This study presents a machine learning-based approach using dark-field microscopy to detect molecular targets by analyzing scattering signals from two different types of metal nanoparticles, improving sensitivity over conventional intensity-based analysis. The method addresses limitations in detecting subtle color and intensity changes in nanoparticle aggregates, offering a more robust biosensing strategy.

papers.title: Accelerating inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models via speculative decoding.
papers.abstract: Genomic and protein foundation models (GFMs and PFMs) have demonstrated strong performance in learning the language of DNA and proteins, but their use in large-scale sequence generation is limited by the latency of autoregressive decoding. Because every token triggers a forward pass of a large Transformer, whose inference is relatively slow, long-sequence generation quickly becomes costly.
papers.summary: This paper introduces speculative decoding to accelerate inference in genomic and proteomic foundation models, addressing the latency bottleneck of autoregressive generation. By using a draft model to propose tokens and the large model to verify them in parallel, the method speeds up sequence generation without compromising output quality.

papers.title: Transformers for molecular property prediction: domain adaptation efficiently improves performance.
papers.abstract: Over the past six years, molecular transformer models have become a part of the computational toolbox for drug discovery. Most existing models are pre-trained on millions to billions of molecules from large-scale unlabeled datasets such as ZINC or ChEMBL. However, the extent to which such large-scale pre-training improves molecular property prediction remains unclear. This study investigates the potential of transformer models for molecular property prediction while addressing their current limitations. We explore strategies to enhance performance, including the influence of pre-training datas
papers.summary: This study investigates whether large-scale pre-training of molecular transformer models improves molecular property prediction for drug discovery. The authors find that domain adaptation—fine-tuning on task-relevant data—efficiently boosts performance, addressing limitations of generic pre-training.

papers.title: An ML-Based QSAR Web Server for KEAP1 Inhibitor Bioactivity Prediction: Composite-Score-Driven Training and Advanced Validation.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular disorders and neurodegenerative diseases are among the leading causes of death worldwide, with oxidative stress being a prominent etiological factor in their development. Lowering chronic oxidative stress has been proposed as a strategy for improving or treating these conditions. The body does this naturally through the KEAP1:NRF2 pathway in healthy individuals. Inhibiting the KEAP1 regulatory protein releases the NRF2 transcription factor, leading to the biosynthesis of the antioxidant proteins. Novel molecules that activate this pathway have recently been proposed as potential
papers.summary: This paper presents a new ML-based QSAR web server for predicting the bioactivity of KEAP1 inhibitors, which are relevant for treating oxidative stress-related diseases. The model uses a composite-score-driven training approach and advanced validation, providing a publicly accessible tool for drug discovery.

papers.title: Histology-derived prediction of a stromal remodeling program in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma with transcriptomic and spatial validation.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate a histology-based model for predicting a stromal stiffness-related molecular surrogate in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) and to assess its spatial biological plausibility.
papers.summary: This study develops a histology-based model to predict a molecular surrogate for stromal stiffness in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), and validates it using transcriptomic and spatial data. The model shows spatial biological plausibility, suggesting that routine histology could serve as a proxy for molecular stromal remodeling programs.

papers.title: Deep learning-based prediction of drug-target interactions between antiviral drugs and SARS-CoV-2 proteins using an image-based representation approach.
papers.abstract: Drug repurposing offers a time-efficient strategy for identifying therapeutics against emerging pathogens such as SARS-CoV-2. In this study, we apply MPS2IT-DTI (Molecule and Protein Sequence to Image Transformer for Drug-Target Interaction), a deep learning framework that represents molecular (SMILES) and protein (FASTA) sequences as images using k-mer frequency encoding, enabling convolutional neural networks to capture spatial compositional patterns associated with biochemical interactions. A curated dataset (BindingDB-FDA) containing 83,165 binding interactions from 1640 FDA-approved ligan
papers.summary: This study applies a deep learning framework (MPS2IT-DTI) that converts drug and protein sequences into images using k-mer frequency encoding, then uses convolutional neural networks to predict drug-target interactions. The model was trained on FDA-approved drug binding data and applied to predict interactions between antiviral drugs and SARS-CoV-2 proteins, offering a computational approach for drug repurposing.

papers.title: Polus: A context-aware enhancement framework for DNA storage via Transformer-based soft-decision decoding.
papers.abstract: DNA storage offers exceptional information density and archival longevity but is constrained by complex biochemical noise inherent to synthesis, storage, and sequencing. Conventional hard-decision error-correction schemes often rely on excessive redundancy to mitigate these imperfections, which significantly compromises storage efficiency and density.
papers.summary: This paper introduces Polus, a framework that uses a Transformer-based soft-decision decoder to improve error correction in DNA storage systems. By leveraging context-aware information, Polus reduces the need for excessive redundancy, thereby enhancing storage efficiency and density while maintaining data integrity.

papers.title: Multivalent ion binding site identification with structure-based deep learning.
papers.abstract: Protein-ion interactions are essential for many cellular processes, including enzymatic catalysis, signaling, and allosteric regulation. However, mapping ion-binding sites experimentally remains labor-intensive and expensive. Here, we present BiteNetI, a structure-based deep learning model that uses 3D convolutional neural networks to simultaneously localize ion-binding centers and predict binding residues for 14 biologically relevant ions. Trained on a carefully curated dataset of over 10,000 high-resolution protein-ion complexes, in which near-identical binding sites are consistently annotat
papers.summary: BiteNetI is a new deep learning tool that predicts where 14 different biologically relevant ions bind to proteins, using only the protein's 3D structure. It identifies both the ion-binding centers and the specific amino acid residues involved, which could help researchers study ion-related functions without costly experiments.

papers.title: Design of Synthesizable PROTACs through Synthesis Constrained Generative Model and Reinforcement Learning.
papers.abstract: Proteolysis targeting chimeras (PROTACs) have emerged as a promising technology in degrading disease-related proteins for drug design. Recent deep generative models can accelerate PROTAC design, but the generated molecules are often difficult to synthesize. Here, we develop the SynPROTAC model, which integrates chemical reaction path-driven molecule assembly with reinforcement learning for the design of synthesizable PROTACs together with favorable binding properties. Specifically, the synthesis-constrained generative model employs a Graph Transformer-encoded warhead or E3 ligand as input and
papers.summary: The authors developed SynPROTAC, a generative model that combines synthesis-constrained molecule assembly with reinforcement learning to design PROTACs that are both synthesizable and have favorable binding properties. This addresses a key limitation of prior deep generative models that often produce hard-to-synthesize molecules.

papers.title: Pansoma, a machine learning tool for identifying somatic variants using pangenome graphs.
papers.abstract: Somatic variant calling, the identification of mutations in non-germline cells acquired over an individual's lifetime, is critical for studying diseases, including cancer, and for developing precision oncology strategies. Traditional somatic variant calling methods rely on linear reference genomes, which do not adequately capture human genetic diversity and result in reference bias, compromising the accuracy of somatic variant detection. Recently developed graph-based human pangenome reference represents diverse genetic variants across human populations and has promised to drive advances in ma
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Pansoma is a new machine learning tool that identifies somatic variants using pangenome graphs, which better capture human genetic diversity than linear reference genomes. By reducing reference bias, it improves the accuracy of somatic variant detection, which is critical for cancer research and precision oncology.

papers.title: SimBinder-IF: Structure-Aware Antibody Affinity Optimization via Efficient Preference Learning.
papers.abstract: Antibody therapeutic efficacy depends on high-affinity target engagement, yet laboratory affinity maturation is slow and costly. Most protein language models (PLMs) lack explicit training for high affinity, and current preference optimization methods introduce computational overhead without clear affinity improvements. Therefore, structure-aware and parameter-efficient approaches for antibody affinity optimization are urgently needed.
papers.summary: This paper introduces SimBinder-IF, a structure-aware method for optimizing antibody affinity using efficient preference learning. It addresses the limitations of existing protein language models and preference optimization methods by incorporating structural information and reducing computational overhead, offering a more effective approach for therapeutic antibody development.

papers.title: EcoXAI: Autonomous Agentic Ecosystem for Explainable Artificial Intelligence and Biomedical Discovery.
papers.abstract: As biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs continue to grow in size, complexity, and heterogeneity, navigating and extracting actionable insights from them presents a major bottleneck for researchers. There is a clear need for autonomous analytical solutions that can utilize recent advancements in agentic AI such as agent harnessing and loop engineering without introducing hallucination or workflow fragmentation. Researchers, regardless of technical expertise, need tools that streamline complex data analysis and deliver meaningful, actionable insights grounded in both data and established bio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: EcoXAI is a new autonomous agentic AI ecosystem designed to help researchers navigate complex biomedical datasets and knowledge graphs. It leverages recent advances in agentic AI to streamline data analysis and deliver actionable insights while aiming to reduce hallucination and workflow fragmentation.

papers.title: The limits of bio-molecular modeling with large language models: a cross-scale evaluation.
papers.abstract: The modeling of bio-molecular system across molecular scales remains a central challenge in scientific research. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to bio-molecular discovery, yet systematic evaluation across multi-scale biological problems and rigorous assessment of their tool-augmented capabilities remain limited.
papers.summary: This paper systematically evaluates the performance of large language models (LLMs) on bio-molecular modeling tasks across different molecular scales, revealing their current limitations and the limited benefit of tool augmentation. The findings provide a critical benchmark for researchers considering LLMs in bio-molecular discovery.

papers.title: Auditing widely used biomolecular benchmarks reveals systematic data inconsistencies.
papers.abstract: Machine learning accelerates molecular discovery and relies heavily on standardised benchmark datasets to evaluate computational performance. To learn transferable structure-activity relationships (SARs), models must be trained on datasets that accurately reflect chemical and biological realities without introducing artificial redundancies. Although standardised benchmarks are ubiquitous, the integrity of their underlying data is often assumed rather than rigorously verified. Currently, there is a lack of systematic and quantitative assessments of hidden data leakage and structural inconsisten
papers.summary: This paper audits widely used biomolecular benchmark datasets and reveals systematic data inconsistencies, including hidden data leakage and structural redundancies that can compromise the training and evaluation of machine learning models. The findings highlight the need for rigorous data integrity checks to ensure reliable structure-activity relationship learning.

papers.title: Omics Data Discovery Agents: Agent-Supported Retrieval, Reanalysis, and Synthesis of Published Omics Data.
papers.abstract: The biomedical literature contains a vast collection of omics studies, yet most published data remain functionally inaccessible for computational reuse. When raw data are deposited in public repositories, essential information for reproducing reported results is dispersed across main text, supplementary files, and code repositories, and in the rarer cases where intermediate data (e.g. protein abundance files) are shared, their location is irregular. Here we present an agentic framework for the agent-supported retrieval, reanalysis, and synthesis of published omics data. The system employs larg
papers.summary: This paper introduces an agentic framework that uses large language models to automatically retrieve, reanalyze, and synthesize published omics data from the literature and public repositories. It addresses the challenge of scattered and inconsistently formatted data by enabling agent-supported discovery and reuse, potentially making vast amounts of published omics data computationally accessible.

papers.title: Evolutionary, Neural, or LLM-Driven Heuristic Generation? A Unified Ant Colony Optimization Benchmark for Nature-Inspired Routing Heuristics on the TSP and CVRP.
papers.abstract: Biomimetic optimization transfers biological information-processing mechanisms into computational systems. Ant colony optimization (ACO) is a canonical example: artificial ants functionally abstract pheromone-mediated stigmergy, decentralized exploration, trail decay through algorithmic evaporation, and adaptive path reinforcement. Building on this functional biological analogue, we present a controlled cross-paradigm evaluation of routing-heuristic generation. A standardized interface embeds human-designed rules, the genetic programming hyper-heuristic GHPP, a resource-constrained DeepACO-MLP
papers.summary: This paper presents a unified benchmark for evaluating routing heuristics on the Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) and Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem (CVRP), comparing human-designed rules, genetic programming, and neural/LLM-driven approaches within an ant colony optimization framework. The study provides a controlled cross-paradigm assessment of heuristic generation, highlighting the strengths and trade-offs of each approach.

papers.title: ProteinDock: A physics-informed layer to improve protein-protein docking reliability.
papers.abstract: Computational modeling provides geometric insight into protein-protein interactions without requiring the resources of experimentation. However, reliability can be hindered when modeling proteins with distinctive features, such as antibodies, that use flexible, polar-rich loops to bind antigens. We developed ProteinDock, a physics-based tool that can be used in combination with leading modeling programs to improve the reliability of protein-protein docking; this work provides a case study of antibody-antigen interfaces. ProteinDock was layered onto Rosetta for docking unbound experimentally de
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: ProteinDock is a new physics-informed layer that can be added to existing docking programs like Rosetta to improve the reliability of protein-protein docking, particularly for challenging cases such as antibody-antigen interactions involving flexible, polar-rich loops. The tool was validated on antibody-antigen interfaces and shows promise for enhancing computational modeling of such complexes.

papers.title: CovSite: A High-Throughput Blind Covalent Screening Framework for Reactive Site Detection.
papers.abstract: Targeted covalent inhibitors are a powerful, yet underexplored, class of therapeutics, and current computational covalent screeners are constrained in early drug discovery due to the need for prior knowledge of the target site and limited throughput. We present CovSite, a blind covalent screening tool that identifies candidate reactive residues across the entire protein surface, utilizing only the protein structure and electrophile SMILES. CovSite applies a pipeline of four orthogonal physicochemical filters (nucleophile identification, solvent accessibility, environment-dependent deprotonatio
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: CovSite is a new computational tool that screens entire protein surfaces to identify potential reactive sites for covalent drug design without requiring prior knowledge of the target site. It uses only the protein structure and an electrophile SMILES, applying four physicochemical filters to pinpoint candidate reactive residues. This high-throughput approach could accelerate early drug discovery for targeted covalent inhibitors.

papers.title: AI-Driven Approaches for the Detection, Classification, and Surveillance of Viral Pathogens: Current Advances, Challenges, and Future Directions.
papers.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly emerged as a transformative tool in virology, offering new opportunities for the detection, classification, and surveillance of viral pathogens. Recent advances in machine learning, deep neural networks, and multimodal data analysis now enable the identification of viral signatures from genomic sequences, medical images, environmental samples, and social-media-derived epidemiological signals. This review provides a comprehensive overview of state-of-the-art AI methodologies applied to viral pathogen research, with a particular focus on image-based diagn
papers.summary: This review comprehensively examines the application of artificial intelligence in virology, covering detection, classification, and surveillance of viral pathogens using diverse data sources such as genomic sequences, medical images, and environmental samples. It highlights current advances in machine learning and deep learning, discusses challenges, and outlines future directions for AI-driven viral diagnostics and epidemiology.

papers.title: An Analysis of the Nutritional Value of Diets Generated by Large Language Models Under Average User Conditions-3(LM)Diet Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: AI tools are becoming increasingly common, including in areas related to health and diet. However, there are no studies indicating the nutritional value of diets generated by large language models (LLMs). The aim of this study was to analyse the nutritional value of diets generated by three major language models. Methods: Three LLMs were used in the study: ChatGPT, Gemini and Copilot. Using each of these, 35-day meal plans were generated for three energy variants: 2000 kcal, 2500 kcal and 3000 kcal. The meal plans were then analysed using dietary software. Results: All L
papers.summary: This study evaluates the nutritional quality of 35-day meal plans generated by three popular large language models (ChatGPT, Gemini, and Copilot) across three calorie targets. The authors found that the AI-generated diets varied in nutritional adequacy, highlighting both potential benefits and limitations of using LLMs for dietary planning under typical user conditions.

papers.title: FoodScribe: an open-source semantic framework for nutrient estimation from free-text dietary records.
papers.abstract: Efficiently summarizing dietary records at scale remains a persistent bottleneck in nutritional epidemiology. We present FoodScribe, which translates free-text meal descriptions into quantitative nutrient profiles by combining ingredient parsing with nutrient retrieval by querying the USDA FoodData Central (FDC) database. Benchmarked using three LLM providers using Nutribench dataset, FoodScribe completed annotation of 3,807 meal descriptions in 2.5 hours, a task otherwise requiring substantial manual effort from trained nutritionists. FoodScribe achieved accuracy across macronutrient estimati
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: FoodScribe is an open-source tool that automatically converts free-text dietary records into quantitative nutrient profiles by parsing ingredients and querying the USDA FoodData Central database. It completed annotation of 3,807 meal descriptions in 2.5 hours, dramatically reducing manual effort, and achieved good accuracy across macronutrient estimates when benchmarked with multiple LLM providers.

papers.title: Computational identification of antigen-specific T cell groups through generative epitope modeling.
papers.abstract: Single-cell T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing enables high-resolution analysis of TCR diversity and clonal expansion. However, inferring antigen specificity for individual TCRs remains challenging and typically requires costly functional assays. We introduce EpitopeGen, a transformer-based model that generates candidate epitope sequences from TCR sequences, enabling population-level identification of T cell groups with shared predicted antigen specificity. EpitopeGen employs a semi-supervised strategy that searches over 70 billion candidate TCR-epitope pairs and incorporates high-confidence bin
papers.summary: EpitopeGen is a transformer-based model that predicts candidate epitope sequences from T cell receptor (TCR) sequences, enabling population-level identification of T cell groups with shared antigen specificity without costly functional assays. The model uses a semi-supervised strategy over 70 billion candidate TCR-epitope pairs, offering a computational approach to infer antigen specificity from single-cell TCR sequencing data.

papers.title: Phenotypic Diversity in Multiple Sclerosis Can Be Represented by Four Additive Symptom Modules.
papers.abstract: Background: Multiple sclerosis (MS) lacks a single invariant phenotypic core. Patients accumulate heterogeneous combinations of sensory, motor, cognitive, and autonomic impairments over time, reflecting lesions that are disseminated in time and space. Standard scales such as the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS) distribute disability across functional systems, but do not explicitly represent MS phenotype as a mixture of latent symptom modules. Methods: We analyzed 4617 de-identified neurology progress notes from 577 patients with MS at a single academic medical center. A large language m
papers.summary: This study analyzed clinical notes from 577 MS patients using a large language model to identify four additive symptom modules that represent the phenotypic diversity of multiple sclerosis. The findings suggest that MS disability can be decomposed into distinct latent symptom clusters, which may improve patient stratification and personalized treatment approaches.

papers.title: A Length-Adaptive LLM-Enhanced Method for Drug-Target Interaction Prediction.
papers.abstract: Drug-target interaction (DTI) prediction is central to drug repurposing. Although existing methods integrate multi-dimensional features and have achieved certain progress, they rely heavily on molecular structure or graph structure information. This makes it difficult to capture complex biomedical semantic associations, leading to insufficient semantic information. To address this issue, this paper proposes BioLA-DTI, a large language model (LLM)-enhanced method for drug-target interaction prediction. The method leverages LLMs to provide semantic information for drugs and proteins. Furthermore
papers.summary: This paper introduces BioLA-DTI, a method that uses large language models to incorporate biomedical semantic information into drug-target interaction prediction, addressing the limitations of structure-based approaches. By leveraging LLM-generated semantic features, the method improves prediction accuracy, offering a promising tool for drug repurposing.

papers.title: DeepExoMir: A Reproducible RNA Language Model Framework for CLIP-Seq-Supported MicroRNA Target-Site Prioritization.
papers.abstract: MicroRNAs regulate gene expression post-transcriptionally, yet target prediction faces a credibility gap: published methods drop sharply against CLIP-seq-validated negatives. We present DeepExoMir, a deep learning framework integrating frozen RiNALMo RNA language model embeddings with biologically informed features. Under a dual-probe ablation protocol on three miRBench test sets, DeepExoMir reaches mean AU-PRC 0.855, surpassing eight retrained baselines (paired bootstrap p<0.001). Evolutionary conservation and duplex structure prove largely redundant with language-model priors, motivating a s
papers.summary: DeepExoMir is a deep learning framework that combines RNA language model embeddings with biologically informed features to improve microRNA target-site prediction, achieving higher accuracy than eight existing methods on CLIP-seq-validated benchmarks. The study finds that evolutionary conservation and duplex structure features are largely redundant when language model priors are used, simplifying the feature set.

papers.title: NutriSteppe-AI: Development, Architecture, and Explainable Design of a Large Language Model-Driven Chatbot for Personalized Health Menu Generation.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Suboptimal dietary patterns are among the leading modifiable contributors to global morbidity and mortality, particularly in cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), obesity, metabolic syndrome, and hypertension. Digital nutrition platforms have emerged to improve adherence to evidence-based dietary strategies; however, many systems lack structured optimization, processing-aware nutrient profiling, and explainable artificial intelligence (AI) mechanisms. The integration of large language models (LLMs) into digital health introduces conversational personal
papers.summary: This paper describes the development and architecture of NutriSteppe-AI, a large language model-driven chatbot designed to generate personalized health menus. It emphasizes the integration of structured optimization, processing-aware nutrient profiling, and explainable AI mechanisms to improve adherence to evidence-based dietary strategies for conditions like cardiovascular disease and type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: A parallel dual-stream state-space module for reliable and efficient biomedical relation extraction.
papers.abstract: Automated drug-drug interaction (DDI) extraction is a cornerstone of global pharmacovigilance, yet its progress is stymied by a fundamental linguistic paradox: relations are signaled by localized morphological cues while being governed by long-range semantic logic. Current monolithic architectures, including Transformer-based models, often face challenges in resolving this feature entanglement, where local clinical descriptors often distort the distal logical chain, leading to noise propagation and reasoning failures. To address this, we present DuSSM, a parallel state-space framework that str
papers.summary: This paper introduces DuSSM, a parallel dual-stream state-space model for biomedical relation extraction, specifically drug-drug interactions. It addresses the challenge of combining local morphological cues with long-range semantic logic, showing improved reliability and efficiency over monolithic architectures like Transformers.

papers.title: An explainable machine learning model for predicting in-hospital infection in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus.
papers.abstract: Infection is a leading cause of mortality in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), yet effective tools for early identification of high-risk patients are lacking. This study aimed to develop an explainable machine learning (ML) model to predict in-hospital infection risk among SLE patients. We analyzed adult patients (≥18 years) with SLE (n = 7,833) from three departments using a population-based electronic medical record database (2000-2024). Among them, 3,157 (40.3%) patients developed an infection after 72 h of hospitalization. An initial comprehensive variable pool of 108 candi
papers.summary: This study developed an explainable machine learning model to predict in-hospital infection risk in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), using a large electronic medical record cohort. The model identifies high-risk patients early, which could help reduce infection-related mortality in SLE.

papers.title: Unveiling the power of TIIC: A prognostic tool for esophageal adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Esophageal adenocarcinoma (EAC) remains a lethal malignancy with limited prognostic tools for guiding immunotherapy. Tumor-infiltrating immune cells (TIICs) play a critical role in EAC prognosis and treatment response.
papers.summary: This paper introduces TIIC, a prognostic tool for esophageal adenocarcinoma that leverages tumor-infiltrating immune cells to guide immunotherapy decisions. The tool aims to improve outcome prediction in a cancer with limited prognostic options.

papers.title: Integrative cfDNA profiling from low-pass whole-genome sequencing enables tissue-of-origin prediction in cancer.
papers.abstract: Cancer type classification is challenging due to tumor heterogeneity and undefined tissue of origin (TOO), particularly in cancers of unknown primary (CUP) and multiple primary cancers (MPC). Accurate TOO identification is critical for guiding treatment and prognosis. We developed a stacked ensemble machine learning classifier that integrates 11 multidimensional cfDNA features spanning genomic, fragmentomic, methylation/repeat, and microbial signals. Base models were constructed using five algorithms, including Deep Learning, Distributed Random Forest, Gradient Boosting Machine, Generalized Li
papers.summary: The authors developed a stacked ensemble machine learning classifier that integrates 11 multidimensional cell-free DNA (cfDNA) features from low-pass whole-genome sequencing, including genomic, fragmentomic, methylation/repeat, and microbial signals, to predict the tissue of origin in cancer. This approach addresses the challenge of classifying cancers with unknown primary or multiple primary cancers, potentially improving treatment guidance and prognosis.

papers.title: A decoupled alignment kernel for peptide membrane permeability predictions.
papers.abstract: Cyclic peptides are promising modalities for targeting intracellular sites; however, cell-membrane permeability remains a key bottleneck, exacerbated by limited public data and the need for well-calibrated uncertainty. Instead of relying on data-eager complex deep learning architecture, we propose a monomer-aware decoupled global alignment kernel (MD-GAK), which couples chemically meaningful residue-residue similarity with sequence alignment while decoupling local matches from gap penalties. MD-GAK is a relatively simple kernel. To further demonstrate the robustness of our framework, we also i
papers.summary: The authors introduce MD-GAK, a simple kernel-based method for predicting cyclic peptide membrane permeability that couples chemically meaningful residue-residue similarity with sequence alignment while decoupling local matches from gap penalties. This approach avoids data-hungry deep learning models and provides well-calibrated uncertainty, addressing a key bottleneck in cyclic peptide drug development.

papers.title: DeepGeSeq: Deep learning library for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.abstract: Deep learning methods have demonstrated significant potential in genomics, enabling broad applications such as sequence activity prediction, regulatory rule identification, and variant effect quantification. However, their widespread adoption is often hindered by the steep computational learning curve required for model construction, training, and downstream biological interpretation. Here, we introduce DeepGeSeq, a user-friendly Deep-learning library tailored for Genomic Sequence modeling and analysis.
papers.summary: DeepGeSeq is a user-friendly deep learning library designed to lower the barrier for applying deep learning to genomic sequence analysis. It provides streamlined tools for model construction, training, and biological interpretation, making advanced genomic modeling more accessible to researchers.

papers.title: Integrative Genomic Analysis Reveals Molecular and Clinical Disparities between Bladder and Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma in K-MASTER Program.
papers.abstract: The clinical outcome of urothelial carcinoma presents significant variability, reflecting its molecular composition, epidemiologic attributes, and primary site of origin. Despite histological similarities, upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC) and bladder urothelial carcinoma (BLCA) represent two distinct disease entities with disparate treatment responses and mutational patterns.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative genomic analysis from the K-MASTER program to compare molecular and clinical features of bladder cancer (BLCA) and upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC), revealing distinct mutational patterns and treatment responses despite their histological similarity. The findings highlight that these are separate disease entities, which may inform site-specific therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence-based diagnostic model for identifying PTPRZ1-MET fusion in a clinically defined secondary glioblastoma cohort.
papers.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) is an aggressive and highly lethal brain tumor. Secondary glioblastoma (sGBM), which arises through malignant progression from lower-grade diffuse glioma, represents a clinically and biologically distinct subset of GBM. In this disease context, the protein tyrosine phosphatase receptor type Z1-mesenchymal-epithelial transition factor (PTPRZ1-MET; ZM) fusion has emerged as a recurrent oncogenic driver associated with adverse clinical outcomes. In this study, we analyzed 159 patients with sGBM, including 15 ZM-positive and 144 ZM-negative cases, and confirmed that ZM-positive
papers.summary: This study developed an AI-based diagnostic model to identify PTPRZ1-MET (ZM) fusion in secondary glioblastoma (sGBM) patients using clinical and pathological features. The model accurately distinguishes ZM-positive from ZM-negative cases, offering a non-invasive or cost-effective tool to guide targeted therapy decisions in this aggressive brain cancer.

papers.title: Eyettention II: A dual-sequence architecture for modeling fixation location, within-word landing position, and fixation duration in reading.
papers.abstract: The way our eyes move while reading provides valuable insights into both the reader's cognitive processes and the properties of the text. In particular, eye-tracking-while-reading data has been shown to be highly beneficial in various technological applications, such as enhancing and interpreting neural language models and inferring a reader's characteristics. However, these applications often rely on large-scale, data-driven models, which demand extensive eye-tracking datasets that are challenging to obtain due to the resource-intensive nature of data collection. To address the challenge of d
papers.summary: The paper introduces Eyettention II, a dual-sequence architecture that simultaneously models fixation location, within-word landing position, and fixation duration during reading. This approach aims to improve the accuracy and efficiency of eye-tracking prediction, potentially reducing the need for large-scale training data in applications like neural language model enhancement.

papers.title: Accurate prediction of gain- and loss-of-function missense variants in GABAA receptors.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in genes encoding GABAA receptors are involved in the pathophysiology of common and rare epilepsies. Variant effects on channel biophysical function are associated with key clinical characteristics and treatment response. Predicting variant effects is therefore key to improving care for individuals with GABAA receptor-related disorders.
papers.summary: This study presents a method for accurately predicting whether missense variants in GABAA receptor genes cause gain- or loss-of-function effects, which are linked to clinical outcomes in epilepsies. The approach could improve variant interpretation and guide treatment decisions for patients with GABAA receptor-related disorders.

papers.title: EscaPRRS-ORF5: a structure-aware evolutionary framework for prioritizing immune escape-prone variants in porcine reproductive and respiratory syndrome virus.
papers.abstract: Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome Virus (PRRSV) is a rapidly evolving RNA virus causing significant economic losses, posing a formidable challenge to vaccine efficacy due to its high mutational variability and immune escape. As the viral mutants evolve, their ability to sustain in population is driven by a range of host biology factors such as receptor binding, fusion, and uncoating. Existing tools that predict viral fitness and escape propensities rely heavily on extensive, up-to-date sequence data and lack integration of biochemical host interactions, limiting mechanistic underst
papers.summary: This paper presents EscaPRRS-ORF5, a new computational framework that integrates structural information and host interaction factors to predict immune escape-prone variants in PRRSV, addressing limitations of existing sequence-only methods. The approach offers a more mechanistic understanding of viral evolution and could aid vaccine design.

papers.title: Key predictors of mortality in profound hyponatremia beyond the correction rate.
papers.abstract: Current guidelines for hyponatremia recommend slow sodium correction; however, recent large-scale observational studies have associated slow correction with increased mortality. The association between correction rate and mortality can be influenced by numerous factors, including comorbidities, overall condition, and treatment interventions, but this complex interplay remains unclear. We aimed to clarify this association by developing interpretable machine-learning models using detailed clinical features.
papers.summary: This study uses interpretable machine learning to identify key predictors of mortality in profound hyponatremia, moving beyond just the rate of sodium correction. The findings suggest that factors such as comorbidities and overall patient condition play a critical role, potentially explaining conflicting results from previous studies on correction speed.

papers.title: A hybrid deep learning framework for real-time speckle reduction and image enhancement on portable ultrasound systems.
papers.abstract: Speckle patterns in ultrasound images often obscure anatomical details, leading to diagnostic uncertainty. Recently, various deep learning-based techniques have been introduced to effectively suppress speckle; however, their high computational costs pose challenges for low-resource devices, such as portable ultrasound systems.
papers.summary: This paper presents a hybrid deep learning framework designed to reduce speckle noise and enhance ultrasound images in real-time on portable systems, addressing the computational limitations of existing deep learning methods. The framework balances image quality improvement with low computational cost, making it suitable for low-resource devices.

papers.title: Refining Accelerometer-Based Animal Behaviour Classifications With Sequence-Informed Post-Processing.
papers.abstract: Supervised machine learning has been used to detect fine-scale behaviours from animal-borne accelerometers by dividing the continuous sequences of behaviour into discrete segments and classifying each with a distinct behavioural category. This approach, while widely implemented, discards the sequential information available in the temporal ordering of the behavioural series. 'Post-processing' (smoothing and error correction made after the initial classifications) can be used to improve the accuracy of the original predictions by learning from the natural transitions and durations of behaviours
papers.summary: This paper presents a post-processing method that uses sequence information (temporal ordering of behaviors) to improve the accuracy of accelerometer-based animal behavior classifications. By learning natural transitions and durations, the approach corrects errors from initial supervised machine learning predictions, offering a more accurate and biologically realistic behavioral sequence.

papers.title: A Dynamic Prognostic and Adaptive Treatment Framework for Advanced Biliary Tract Cancer.
papers.abstract: First-line immuno-chemotherapy is standard for advanced biliary tract cancer (BTC), but outcomes vary substantially, necessitating longitudinal monitoring and treatment adaptation. We aimed to develop models that dynamically update survival predictions using evolving clinical data to support real-time prognostic stratification.
papers.summary: This study develops dynamic prognostic models for advanced biliary tract cancer that update survival predictions as new clinical data becomes available, enabling real-time risk stratification and adaptive treatment decisions. The approach addresses the variability in patient outcomes under standard first-line immuno-chemotherapy by leveraging longitudinal monitoring.

papers.title: GeneInsight: Condensing gene set knowledge via language models.
papers.abstract: Gene set analysis often returns extensive annotations from multiple sources, requiring manual effort to identify coherent biological themes. We developed GeneInsight, an AI-powered tool that automates this by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering semantically related terms using sentence embeddings, and generating thematic summaries via large language model prompting. This enables researchers to identify biological themes that may be obscured when annotation sources are examined separately.
papers.summary: GeneInsight is an AI-powered tool that automates the interpretation of gene set analysis results by retrieving functional annotations from STRING-DB, clustering semantically related terms, and generating concise thematic summaries using large language models. This helps researchers quickly identify coherent biological themes that might be missed when examining annotation sources separately.

papers.title: The Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool With Artificial Intelligence (START-AI) to Support Decision Making in Emergency Departments: Model Explainability and Feature Importance Analysis.
papers.abstract: Evaluate the importance of specific variables contributing to a recently reported Artificial Intelligence (AI) prediction model called Sydney Triage to Admission Risk Tool with Artificial Intelligence (START-AI) to predict inpatient admission from the Emergency Department (ED).
papers.summary: This study analyzes the feature importance and explainability of START-AI, an AI model that predicts whether emergency department patients will be admitted to the hospital. The authors identify which clinical variables most strongly influence the model's predictions, providing transparency to support clinician trust and decision-making.

papers.title: Unveiling the aging-immune axis in irritable bowel syndrome: a multi-omics and machine learning approach to biomarker discovery and validation.
papers.abstract: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a prevalent functional gastrointestinal disorder with an elusive pathophysiology. Although immune dysregulation and mild mucosal inflammation are recognized as important factors in IBS, the specific contribution of immunosenescence remains unclear. Prior MR studies on IBS focused on single molecular traits; however, an integrated multi-omics framework for aging-immune genes has not been applied. Here, we integrate cis-eQTL/pQTL/mQTL with machine learning and in vivo validation to identify putatively causal biomarkers and unravel the aging-immune axis.
papers.summary: This study integrates multi-omics data (eQTL, pQTL, mQTL) with machine learning to identify aging-related immune biomarkers for irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and validates them in vivo. It uncovers a potential aging-immune axis contributing to IBS pathophysiology, offering new candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Clinically interpretable deep learning for breast cancer missense variant pathogenicity prediction.
papers.abstract: Missense variants in breast cancer remain diagnostically challenging due to their functional diversity and complex genomic contexts. Conventional laboratory assays for evaluating pathogenicity are labor-intensive, costly, and often impractical for large-scale screening, creating a pressing need for accurate, scalable, and clinically interpretable computational approaches.
papers.summary: This paper presents a clinically interpretable deep learning model for predicting the pathogenicity of missense variants in breast cancer, addressing the limitations of labor-intensive laboratory assays. The model aims to provide accurate and scalable predictions while maintaining interpretability for clinical use.

papers.title: Fractal and Machine Learning Analyses of MALDI-TOF Mass Spectrometry Data in Glioblastoma.
papers.abstract: Data preprocessing is a critical step in the analysis of matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization-time-of-flight mass spectrometry (MALDI-TOF MS) spectra for machine learning applications, typically involving steps such as spectra trimming, baseline correction, smoothing, transformation, and peak picking or spectral binning. While traditional approaches focus on protein/peptide peaks as features, this study explores a novel method of feature extraction by treating MALDI-TOF spectra as one-dimensional signal array further processed as time-series data. This study investigates the use of comp
papers.summary: This study explores a novel approach to analyzing MALDI-TOF mass spectrometry data from glioblastoma by treating spectra as time-series signals and applying fractal analysis combined with machine learning. The method offers an alternative to traditional peak-based feature extraction, potentially improving classification or diagnostic accuracy.

papers.title: Machine learning-driven risk assessment of severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae in children: analysis based on core clinical and immunological features.
papers.abstract: To construct and validate an interpretable machine learning model for early prediction of severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP) in children.
papers.summary: This study develops an interpretable machine learning model using core clinical and immunological features to predict severe Mycoplasma pneumoniae pneumonia (SMPP) in children, aiming to enable early risk assessment. The model provides a practical tool for clinicians to identify high-risk pediatric patients and improve timely intervention.

papers.title: Explainable machine learning for predicting venous thromboembolism in septic shock patients.
papers.abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) frequently complicates septic shock, yet precise, individualized risk stratification tools remain scarce. This study aimed to develop and externally validate an explainable machine learning (ML) framework to predict VTE in this critically ill population.
papers.summary: This study developed and externally validated an explainable machine learning framework to predict venous thromboembolism (VTE) in septic shock patients, addressing the need for individualized risk stratification in this high-risk population. The model's explainability features likely enhance clinical interpretability and trust, potentially improving VTE prevention strategies.

papers.title: Resveratrol Nanoformulations for Cancer Management: A Comprehensive Review of Disease-Specific Strategies and Clinical Translational Barriers.
papers.abstract: Cancer remains a leading cause of mortality worldwide, highlighting the need for therapeutic strategies that reduce systemic toxicity and drug resistance. Resveratrol (RES), a natural polyphenolic stilbenoid, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, pro-apoptotic, anti-metastatic, and chemosensitizing activities. However, its clinical translation is limited by poor aqueous solubility, chemical instability, rapid metabolic clearance, and consequently low systemic bioavailability. Nanotechnology-based drug delivery systems provide a promising strategy to address these limitations. This review s
papers.summary: This review examines resveratrol nanoformulations for cancer therapy, highlighting their potential to overcome the drug's poor bioavailability and enhance its anticancer effects. It discusses disease-specific strategies and identifies key clinical translational barriers, such as manufacturing scalability and regulatory hurdles.

papers.title: Refining sequence-to-activity models by increasing model resolution.
papers.abstract: Decoding the cis-regulatory syntax that controls gene expression is essential for improving our understanding of cell differentiation and disease. Deep learning based sequence-to-activity (S2A) models learn to identify regulatory motifs and their syntax through modeling chromatin accessibility. Previously, we developed AI-TAC, a S2A model that predicts chromatin accessibility across various immune cell types in multi-task fashion, effectively decoding the regulatory syntax underlying immune cell differentiation. While ATAC-seq is commonly used to measure regional accessibility, it also provide
papers.summary: This paper refines sequence-to-activity (S2A) models by increasing model resolution to better decode cis-regulatory syntax controlling gene expression. The authors extend their previous AI-TAC model, which predicts chromatin accessibility across immune cell types, by leveraging higher-resolution ATAC-seq data to improve the accuracy of regulatory motif and syntax identification.

papers.title: Interpretable machine learning identifies a clinically inferred inflammasome-associated inflammatory injury phenotype in children with adenovirus pneumonia.
papers.abstract: Severe adenovirus pneumonia in children is characterized by persistent fever, systemic inflammation, and extrapulmonary tissue injury. Although adenovirus can activate inflammasome pathways, direct inflammasome biomarkers are not routinely available in pediatric practice. This study developed an interpretable machine-learning framework for retrospective severity discrimination and inflammatory phenotype stratification.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study uses interpretable machine learning on retrospective pediatric data to identify a clinically inferred inflammasome-associated inflammatory injury phenotype in children with severe adenovirus pneumonia, enabling severity discrimination without direct inflammasome biomarkers. The approach provides a practical framework for stratifying inflammatory phenotypes in clinical settings.

papers.title: Cross-scale modeling reveals a TFRC-driven immunosuppressive macrophage niche in cervical cancer.
papers.abstract: The functional plasticity of tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) is a critical determinant of the immunosuppressive microenvironment in cervical cancer, yet its integration into actionable prognostic frameworks remains limited. This study aimed to establish a TAM polarization-centered model and elucidate the mechanisms of underlying tumor-immune crosstalk.
papers.summary: This study develops a cross-scale model centered on tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) polarization in cervical cancer, identifying a TFRC-driven immunosuppressive macrophage niche that contributes to the tumor's immune evasion. The findings provide a prognostic framework and mechanistic insight into tumor-immune crosstalk, potentially guiding future therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Application of deep learning in prognostic prediction of non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is characterized by high heterogeneity. Traditional prognostic evaluation methods such as TNM staging are difficult to accurately characterize the survival differences of patients, and there is an urgent clinical need for more efficient individualized prediction tools. With its powerful automatic feature extraction and nonlinear modeling capabilities, deep learning has shown significant advantages in the processing of multimodal medical data and has become a core technical direction in NSCLC prognosis research. This paper reviews the research progress of deep
papers.journal: Frontiers in cell and developmental biology
papers.summary: This review summarizes recent advances in using deep learning for prognostic prediction in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), highlighting its advantages over traditional methods like TNM staging in handling multimodal medical data. The authors position deep learning as a core technical direction for developing more individualized survival prediction tools.

papers.title: Foundation model-enhanced multimodal radiomics for predicting response to chemo-immunotherapy in advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma.
papers.abstract: To develop and validate a foundation model-driven multimodal fusion framework for non-invasive prediction of treatment response to first-line chemo-immunotherapy in patients with advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC).
papers.summary: This study presents a foundation model-enhanced multimodal radiomics framework that integrates imaging data with clinical information to non-invasively predict how patients with advanced lung squamous cell carcinoma will respond to first-line chemo-immunotherapy. The approach shows promise for improving treatment personalization by identifying likely non-responders before therapy begins.

papers.title: Pooling multimodal cancer data across unaligned embedding spaces maintains tumor of origin signal.
papers.abstract: AI-based embeddings offer the possibilities of encoding complex biological data into low-dimensional spaces, called embedding spaces, that maintain the relationships between entities. Vector pooling is the process of aggregating an array of embedded vectors, either usually by summing or averaging, to summarize the total movement with the embedding space. Embedded vector pooling allows sampling of an arbitrary number of points to be summarized into a fixed sized vector, and is frequently used to sample networks of embedded values or to summarize protein language model vectors. There is an open
papers.summary: This paper investigates whether pooling multimodal cancer data across unaligned embedding spaces can preserve tumor-of-origin signal. The authors likely demonstrate that simple vector pooling methods (e.g., averaging) can effectively combine embeddings from different data types without requiring alignment, maintaining biological signal. This provides a practical approach for integrating heterogeneous cancer datasets.

papers.title: Object-centric diffusion policies for real-world robotic-arm imitation learning.
papers.abstract: Imitation learning in complex, unstructured environments remains challenging due to the difficulty of grounding perception in physically meaningful representations and the need to model multimodal action distributions. Existing approaches often rely on unstructured pixel-level feature encodings or stochastic latent-variable decoders, which can lead to brittle attention in cluttered scenes. In this work, we present a novel integration of detector-based visual representations with conditional diffusion modeling (DINO + CDP) for real-world robotic imitation learning. Our framework utilizes a DINO
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel integration of detector-based visual representations (DINO) with conditional diffusion modeling for robotic-arm imitation learning, addressing challenges in complex, unstructured environments. The approach improves grounding of perception and models multimodal action distributions, leading to more robust performance in real-world cluttered scenes.

papers.title: mwHIT: accelerated and accurate histone modification imputation using multi-scale window attention.
papers.abstract: Histone modifications regulate chromatin organization and gene activity, and abnormal modification patterns are closely associated with disease-related transcriptional dysregulation. Although ChIP-seq provides accurate measurements of histone modification profiles, genome-wide experimental profiling remains costly and time-consuming. Here, we propose mwHIT, a multi-scale window attention-based Histone Modification Imputation Transformer that predicts histone modification signals from run-on sequencing (RO-seq) and DNA sequence features. mwHIT captures both local and long-range regulatory infor
papers.summary: mwHIT is a new deep-learning tool that predicts histone modification signals from run-on sequencing (RO-seq) and DNA sequence data using a multi-scale window attention mechanism. It accurately imputes histone modification profiles, capturing both local and long-range regulatory information, and offers a faster and more cost-effective alternative to experimental ChIP-seq profiling.

papers.title: Deciphering tuberculosis pathway mechanisms via graph neural networks and multimodal deep learning: a comprehensive AI-driven framework for precision medicine.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) remains a global health crisis, with complex molecular mechanisms that are not fully understood. Traditional pathway analysis methods fail to capture the intricate non-linear relationships within biological networks.
papers.summary: This paper presents a novel AI framework that combines graph neural networks with multimodal deep learning to analyze tuberculosis (TB) pathway mechanisms, capturing non-linear relationships that traditional methods miss. The approach aims to improve precision medicine for TB by providing a more comprehensive understanding of the disease's molecular underpinnings.
